learn: A browser (client) requests pages from a web server.
Servers respond with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images and data.
HTTP is the protocol; HTTPS encrypts it.
lessons.try: Diagram what happens when you visit a website.

learn: A URL has a protocol, domain, path and sometimes a query.
DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.
Domains are registered and renewed yearly.
lessons.try: Break five URLs into their parts.

learn: HTML structures content, CSS styles it, JavaScript adds behaviour.
Keep each layer in its own file when possible.
Browser developer tools let you inspect each layer.
lessons.try: Open developer tools and inspect a web page.

learn:
Elements have opening and closing tags:

text

.

Some are void (empty): ,
.
Attributes add information: <a href="page.html">.
lessons.try: Write a page with headings, paragraphs and a link.

learn: Every page starts with <!DOCTYPE html>, then <html>, <head> and <body>.
The head holds the title, metadata and stylesheet links.
The body holds visible content.
lessons.try: Write a valid HTML skeleton from memory.

learn: Lists: <ul> (bullets), <ol> (numbers), <li> (items).
Images need alt text for accessibility.
Tables use <table>, <tr>, <th>, <td> for data, not layout.
lessons.try: Build a page with a list, image and table.

learn: Semantic tags describe meaning: <header>, <nav>, <main>, <article>, <section>, <footer>.
They help screen readers and search engines.
Use <div> only when no semantic tag fits.
lessons.try: Rewrite a div-only page with semantic tags.

learn: Use one <h1> per page and nested headings in order.
<strong> and <em> add meaning, not just style.
Write clear, scannable content.
lessons.try: Outline a page with correct heading levels.

learn: Forms collect input: <form>, <input>, <label>, <button>, <select>, <textarea>.
Every input needs a label.
Input types like email and number help validation.
lessons.try: Build a contact form with labels.

learn: A rule has a selector and declarations: p { color: navy; }.
Select by element, class (.card) or id (#main).
Link stylesheets with <link rel="stylesheet">.
lessons.try: Style a page with element and class selectors.

learn: Later rules override earlier ones of equal specificity.
Specificity: id beats class, class beats element.
Inheritance passes some properties (like color) to children.
check: Which wins: a class or an element selector?
lessons.try: Predict which rule wins in five examples.

learn: Colours: names, hex (#336699), rgb() and hsl().
Fonts: font-family, font-size, line-height.
Units: px (fixed), rem and em (relative), % and vw (viewport).
check: rem units are relative to the...
lessons.try: Create a colour and type style guide for a site.

learn: Every element is a box: content, padding, border, margin.
box-sizing: border-box includes padding and border in the width.
Margins create space between boxes.
lessons.try: Inspect the box model in developer tools.

learn: display: flex arranges children in a row or column.
justify-content aligns along the main axis; align-items along the cross axis.
gap adds space between items.
check: Flexbox arranges items in a row or...
lessons.try: Build a navigation bar with flexbox.

learn: display: grid creates rows and columns.
grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) makes three equal columns.
Grid suits two-dimensional layouts; flexbox suits one dimension.
check: fr means a ___ of free space.
lessons.try: Lay out a photo gallery with CSS Grid.

learn: Design for small screens first, then add styles for larger ones.
Include <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">.
Most web traffic is now on phones.
check: Mobile-first means designing for ___ screens first.
The viewport meta tag helps pages fit...
lessons.try: Test a page at phone, tablet and desktop widths.

learn: @media (min-width: 600px) { ... } applies styles above 600 px.
Breakpoints are where the layout changes.
Choose breakpoints based on content, not specific devices.
lessons.try: Add two breakpoints to a layout.

learn: img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; } keeps images inside their containers.
Use srcset to serve smaller images to small screens.
Test on real devices when possible.
lessons.try: Make all images on your site responsive.

learn: Accessibility means everyone, including people with disabilities, can use a site.
WCAG guidelines: perceivable, operable, understandable, robust.
Keyboard navigation and screen reader support are essential.
check: WCAG stands for Web Content ___ Guidelines.
Sites should work with only a...
lessons.try: Navigate a site using only the keyboard.

learn: Text needs a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text.
Use readable fonts at 16 px or larger for body text.
Don't rely on colour alone to convey meaning.
check: Normal text needs contrast of at least...
Body text is often at least...
Don't rely on ___ alone for meaning.
lessons.try: Check your site's colours with a contrast checker.

learn: Alignment, contrast, repetition and proximity organise a page.
White space improves clarity.
Consistent navigation helps users.
lessons.try: Redesign a cluttered page using the four principles.

learn: Declare with let and const; avoid var.
Types: number, string, boolean, null, undefined, object, array.
Use === for strict equality.
check: A value that never changes uses...
lessons.try: Write a script that logs variables of each type.

learn: function add(a, b) { return a + b; } or arrow form: const add = (a, b) => a + b.
if/else and loops (for, while) work like other languages.
Arrays have methods: push, map, filter, forEach.
lessons.try: Write a function that returns the largest number in an array.

learn: Objects store key-value pairs: { name: "Ana", age: 16 }.
Access with dot notation: person.name.
JSON is a text format for data, based on JavaScript objects.
lessons.try: Create an object for a book and log each property.

learn: The DOM represents a page as a tree of objects.
document.querySelector("#id") selects elements.
Change content with textContent and styles with classList.
check: The DOM represents a page as a...
lessons.try: Change a heading's text with JavaScript.

learn: addEventListener("click", handler) responds to user actions.
Common events: click, input, submit, keydown.
The event object holds details about what happened.
lessons.try: Make a button that counts clicks.

learn: Read input values with element.value.
Validate before using data; show helpful error messages.
preventDefault() stops a form from reloading the page.
lessons.try: Validate a sign-up form with JavaScript.

learn: Define the purpose, audience and pages.
Sketch wireframes and a site map before coding.
Gather content and credit images.
lessons.try: Write a project brief and draw a site map.

learn: Git tracks changes to files over time.
Commit often with clear messages.
Hosting services store repositories online for collaboration.
lessons.try: Create a repository and make five commits.

learn: Free static hosting services can publish HTML, CSS and JavaScript sites.
Test in several browsers and screen sizes.
Check accessibility, broken links and load speed before launch.
check: Static sites use HTML, CSS and...
lessons.try: Publish your website and share it with the class.
